summary: The Moon in Aries (Mars's sign, neutral for the Moon) gives a quick, restless, courageous and proud mind. Texts describe a lively, impulsive person, popular with others, whose finances can be unsteady.
common_outcomes: Restless, fond of travel and movement
Brave and self-respecting; values honour over money
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 17.1: eldest among siblings; marks or scars on the head; fear of water
Saravali 23.1: no siblings (contrasting with BJ's 'eldest'); many sons; easily won over by women
Phaladeepika 9.1 (Aries rising/Moon): eats little, always on the move, tends to bend the truth

by_area.personality: Quick to understand, restless and heroic (Brihat Jataka 17.1); valorous, self-respecting and fickle (Saravali 23.1); impulsive, irritable, enterprising, haughty and restless (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Raman HPA ch. XXII: enterprising and dexterous but subordinate in position.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 17.1: unstable wealth; Saravali 23.1: lasting wealth.
by_area.health: Texts mention weak knees or legs and head wounds (Brihat Jataka 17.1; Saravali 23.1) as traditional bodily markers; do not use as predictions.
by_area.relationships: Won over by women (Saravali 23.1); popular and fond of women (Raman).
by_area.family: Brihat Jataka 17.1 makes the native the eldest sibling while Saravali 23.1 says without co-born; Saravali adds more sons.

Mercury's aspect (Saravali 23.2-7: teaching and poetic fame)

Mars's aspect (Saravali 23.2-7: eye/teeth trouble and wounds)
Waning or dim Moon, which Braha (pp. 19-20) treats as malefic and weaker

phrasing_guidance: Describe an energetic, brave, quick-reacting mind that benefits from patience. Avoid bodily-mark or water-fear claims unless asked about classical texts.

summary: The Moon is exalted in Taurus (deepest exaltation at 3°), and per BPHS the rest of Taurus (about 4-30°) is its moolatrikona. It gives a calm, patient, generous and attractive temperament with growing happiness in middle and later life.
common_outcomes: Happiness and stability increase in middle and later life
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 17.2 and Saravali 23.8: more daughters
Brihat Jataka 17.2: some separation from early relatives or family wealth
Phaladeepika 9.2: work connected with agriculture or cattle

by_area.personality: Self-denying, enduring and authoritative (Brihat Jataka 17.2); large-hearted, charitable, discerning and forbearing (Saravali 23.8); liberal, intelligent, of sound judgment but a wavering mind (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Agriculture and cattle (Phaladeepika 9.2); Raman: ability to command, influential.
by_area.finance: Raman HPA ch. XXII: rich and lucky; Phaladeepika 9.14 (any exalted planet): wealth and treasures.
by_area.health: Brihat Jataka 17.2 mentions strong digestion and a kapha constitution; present only as a temperament note.
by_area.relationships: Raman HPA ch. XXII: popular, fond of the opposite sex, influenced by women, love intrigues.
by_area.family: Classical texts mention more daughters (Brihat Jataka 17.2; Saravali 23.8); confirm from the 5th house before saying so.
by_area.spirituality: Brihat Jataka 17.2 calls the native self-denying.

source_views.view: The fallen Moon harms the overall tenor of the chart and is read harshly in every house; neechabhanga arises when an exalted planet joins it, its sign lord is exalted or in a kendra from lagna or Moon.

disagreements: Classical verses are mostly unfavourable, yet Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika also mention a respected family or royal honour. Modern practitioners give a more psychological, growth-oriented reading. Commentators differ on whether the 'exaltation lord' for cancellation is Venus (lord of Taurus) or the planet exalted in Scorpio (none in the standard scheme). Braha reads the fallen Moon harshly in every house, while Frawley says cancellation is possible and a cancelled Moon in Scorpio gives psychological depth; Frawley's angle rule and Braha's angle readings conflict directly for the 1st, 4th, 7th and 10th houses. BPHS treats all of Scorpio as debilitation, while Braha (p. 47) says that past 3 degrees the Moon is technically no longer fallen.
phrasing_guidance: Never call the person cruel or secretive. Say the emotional nature is deep and protective, and that supports in the chart (cancellation, Jupiter) matter a lot. No health or parental-loss predictions.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, ch. 'The Signs: How Planets Transmit Influences of the Stars', p. 127
source_views.view: Vedic astrology has no 'detriment'; the Moon in Capricorn can be considered favourable because only from there does it aspect its own sign, Cancer.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Moon' pp. 19-21, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: A waxing, bright Moon is benefic and stronger and a waning, dim one malefic; the chart is also read from the Moon (Chandra lagna); the Moon has directional strength in the 4th; planets in kendras are powerful and in dusthanas spoiled.

disagreements: Saravali calls the native truthful and charitable while Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika stress hypocrisy; all agree on endurance and fortune. Frawley (p. 127) treats the Moon in Capricorn as favourable because it aspects its own sign Cancer, a structural argument the classical sign verses do not make.
phrasing_guidance: Present as practical, loyal and enduring. Do not repeat moral labels (hypocrite, shameless); frame as a reminder to keep values and actions aligned.

summary: The Moon in Aquarius is in Saturn's other sign (neutral). Texts describe a tireless traveller with fluctuating fortunes, fond of perfumes, flowers and friends, but warn of a restless, rule-bending streak.
common_outcomes: Enjoys travel and is tireless on journeys
Fond of friends, perfumes and flowers
rare_outcomes: Saravali 23.72: artisan; diseased eyes; very poor
Brihat Jataka 17.11: signs of frailty in later years
Phaladeepika 9.11: skilled at harming rivals; greedy

by_area.personality: Secretive wrongdoing (Phaladeepika 9.11) and aversion to the virtuous (Saravali 23.72) in the classical verses; Raman HPA ch. XXII gives beautiful-minded, artistic, inoffensive and grateful, with a tendency to hypocrisy.
by_area.career: Artisan (Saravali 23.72); endures long journeys (Phaladeepika 9.11); Raman: artistic taste, esoteric interests.
by_area.finance: Gains and losses alternate (Brihat Jataka 17.11; Phaladeepika 9.11); Saravali 23.72: very poor; Raman: sudden rises and falls.
by_area.relationships: Brihat Jataka 17.11 cautions about involvement in others' partners or wealth; handle gently.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 23.72: averse to conventional virtue; Raman: esoteric and mystical.

Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 23.73-78: land and estates)
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 23.73-78: property and wealth)
Mercury's aspect (Saravali 23.73-78: musical skill)
Sun's aspect (Saravali 23.73-78: dignified bearing)

Mars's aspect (Saravali 23.73-78: indolence)
Waning or dim Moon, which Braha (pp. 19-20) treats as malefic and weaker

summary: The Moon in Pisces is in Jupiter's sign (neutral). Texts agree on a learned, attractive, devout and fortunate person who gains through water-related things, wins over opponents and is devoted to the spouse.
common_outcomes: Wealth through water, sea or overseas connections
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 17.12: wealth drawn from a large treasury or others' resources
Saravali 23.79: fond of sailing; serves rulers; skilled in fine arts and music
Phaladeepika 9.12: earns from pearls and sea products; drinks much water

by_area.personality: Polite, somewhat irascible and liberal (Saravali 23.79); grateful (Phaladeepika 9.12); steady, simple and learned (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Pearls and ocean products (Phaladeepika 9.12; Raman: dealer in pearls); serves the king, skilled in fine arts and music, fond of sailing (Saravali 23.79).
by_area.finance: Wealth from water-related sources (Brihat Jataka 17.12; Phaladeepika 9.12); happiness and wealth (Saravali 23.79).
by_area.relationships: Devoted to and influenced by the spouse (Brihat Jataka 17.12; Phaladeepika 9.12; Raman).
by_area.family: Fond of wife and children, many children (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.spirituality: Very religious (Saravali 23.79); Raman: spiritually inclined later in life.
